newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end near highs on bank rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end near highs on bank rise.

text.p: *Stocks ended firm, supported by banks after a bond market rally. Total volume 329.9 million shares, value A$617.0 million, 1,017 stocks traded, 361 steady, 387 rises, 269 falls
Australian shares finished up and near their highs on Wednesday after the influential bank sector benefited from a bond market rally following a surge in U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index closed 13.7 points higher at 2,336.7, near its intra-day high of 2,340.1.
The December share price index finished up 22 points at 2,353 and at a 16.3 point premium to the underlying index.
Bellwether stock, BHP, put in a strong performance, losing just nine cents despite going ex-dividend 25 cents.

"Metal prices were weaker overnight but the only effect on the resource sector today was that they didn't run as high as they possibly could have," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney-based broker, Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said the market focus would remain on the Dow and metal prices, with local interest rates the key to the performance of bank sector.
"Today was no different to normal. The banks have been getting a boost from the bond market once every two or three days. I don't see any change to this situation in the near term," Spiteri said.

Most major banks followed the bond market higher with the largest, National Australia Bank, jumping over two percent to an intraday high of A$13.79, while Westpac Banking Corp closed 12 cents firmer at a record high of A$7.04.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Corp added 1.4 percent to close at A$7.30.
Traders said the rally in bonds, both locally and in the U.S., had provided the impetus for investor's interest in the sector, aided by some switching from resource stocks.
The insurance sector was also stronger with GIO Australia and HIH Winterthur finding healthy buying interest.

In other local markets, Australian bonds ended firmer despite a surprise A$1.69 billion September current account deficit. The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.40 percent, down 0.11 percentage points from Tuesday's levels.
The Australian dollar survived the rise in the country's trade deficit with superficial damage. At 5.20 p.m. (0620 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$7910/15.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivative trade was quiet but steady as the market awaits important U.S. economic data later this week.
